archetypes.name: contract-sync
archetypes.rationale: The plan intentionally changes a published workflow contract across script, sibling contract, skill prose, and structure pins, so drift is the main risk.
archetypes.prompt_body: Compare the proposed order and gating change against the scoped script and documentation surfaces. Look for places where the plan would leave design-publish.md, SKILL.md, or structural assertions describing the old publish-before-rename contract. Pay special attention to whether the reentry marker remains publish-gated while the title rename becomes only SESSION_ID-gated. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: harness-drift
archetypes.rationale: The behavioral change depends on tests flipping several negative-publish cases rather than only the happy-path order.
archetypes.prompt_body: Inspect whether the proposed test updates cover every publish outcome affected by moving the rename before design-log-publish.sh. Check that PUBLISH_OK=false, unexpected publish rc, and missing PUBLISH_OK cases all assert that rename already ran, while marker behavior remains unchanged. Look for stale assertions, log-position comparisons, or regex dependencies that could accidentally keep the old behavior green. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: admission-gate
archetypes.rationale: This plan deliberately changes the temporal admission boundary for /implement, so the reviewer should verify there are no contradictory gates or rollback assumptions.
archetypes.prompt_body: Evaluate the proposed change as an admission-gate move rather than a generic reorder. Check whether any scoped prose or script logic still implies that /implement admission waits for log publishing, publish success, cleanup, or reentry-marker creation. Investigate whether failure handling after a successful early rename could contradict the operator's binding requirement that log flush failure must not affect /implement. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
